newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat says early '97 results above forecast.
newsitem.headline: Fiat says early '97 results above forecast.

text.p: Italian industrial giant Fiat SpA said on Thursday the group had performed ahead of forecasts in the first few months of 1997.
Fiat said in a brief statement released after a board meeting, the most important data for the first few months of the year showed "a positive trend and higher than the forecasts in the budget."
The Turin-based carmaker also said the board had "examined a new forecast regarding the whole of 1997, the data for which will be illustrated at the shareholders' meeting on June 16."

It gave no other details but Fiat chairman Cesare Romiti said at the end of May the group's 1997 sales would be around 90 trillion lire ($53 billion) compared with 78 trillion in 1996, with profits forecast not below last year's.
Fiat made a consolidated net profit of 2.37 trillion in 1996 and first quarter 1997 group sales rose 4.4 percent to 20.844 trillion.
Analysts say the carmaker's turnover has been helped by a new car buying incentive scheme introduced by the Italian government at the start of this year to boost demand in the flagging sector.
Under the scheme owners of cars of over 10 years old can receive a discount if they trade old models in for new. The scheme is set to run until the end of September.
Fiat's new car sales rose 23.3 percent in April compared with an overall increase in European new car sales of 9.2 percent that month.
The Italian group also boosted its market share within Europe to 12.7 percent compared with 11.2 percent in April 1996.
May data for new car registrations in Italy are due to be released by the Ministry of Transport on June 10.
